# READ THIS FIRST — Compliance & Action List

**What this pack is.** A complete set of professionally drafted microlending documents for QuickServe Cashloan (Quickserve Financial Services CC), written in plain English and built around Namibian law — chiefly the **Microlending Act 7 of 2018** and NAMFISA's rules for registered microlenders.

**What this pack is not.** It is **not a legal opinion**, and it is **not ready to hand to a borrower as it stands.** It is a strong first draft that a Namibian attorney must review and sign off before first use. This page tells you, and them, exactly what to check and why.

**One honest limitation you must know about.** The research behind these documents was done in an environment where the primary legal sources — the Act itself on NamibLII and the Legal Assistance Centre site, and NAMFISA's own website — were **blocked and could not be opened first-hand.** Every rule below comes from NAMFISA's consumer-education material and reputable secondary reporting, not from a direct reading of the gazetted text. That is why section numbers and exact figures are flagged for confirmation rather than stated as settled. Treat this page as a well-researched checklist for your lawyer, not as the final word.

---

## 1. STOP-AND-CHECK ITEMS — do not issue any document until these are resolved

1.1 **Are you registered with NAMFISA?** Operating as a microlender without registration is itself the offence — a fine of up to N$500,000 and/or up to five years' imprisonment — and no wording in any document cures it. If Quickserve Financial Services CC is not yet a NAMFISA-registered microlender, that comes first, before anything in this pack is used. **Registration is currently in progress.** Because it has not yet been granted, the documents in this pack have been worded so they do not state or imply that QuickServe is already registered with, or regulated by, NAMFISA. Do not add any such statement, and do not fill in a NAMFISA registration number, until the certificate is actually issued.

1.2 **The 30% rate and the service fee cannot both stand as they are.** In Namibia the 30% ceiling on a short-term microloan is a **once-off** cap on **total finance charges** for the whole loan — not a monthly rate. Critically, "finance charges" is defined to include **everything the borrower pays above the cash advanced**, so a **service fee counts inside the 30%, not on top of it.**

   - A N$1,000 loan at 30% interest (N$300) **plus** a N$50 service fee = N$350 = **35% — over the cap, and the contract itself is the offence** (the law forbids even *stipulating* an over-cap charge, s 22(1)).
   - **Decision you must make now:** either the interest rate and the service fee **together** stay at or below 30% of principal, or you drop the service fee. The documents are drafted around a single "Total finance charges ≤ 30%" line for exactly this reason. Set your numbers so row E of the loan cost table never exceeds 30%.

1.3 **Rollovers / extensions — your single highest legal risk.** Your ledger app currently charges **another full interest cycle** each time a loan is extended. On the same loan, that pushes total finance charges past the 30% ceiling, which is very likely **unlawful**. This pack takes the conservative position — an extension may not push cumulative charges past 30% of principal — but whether *any* further charge is lawful on a rollover, and whether an extension must instead be written up as a **brand-new loan with a fresh affordability check**, is the first question for your attorney and for NAMFISA. The lawful mechanism for an unpaid loan is more likely **default interest** (see 2.1), not a fresh interest cycle.

1.4 **Fix the flyer's wording (done in this repo, confirm you are happy with it).** A bare "30% interest" with no period invites the unlawful reading "30% per month". The flyer has been updated to "30% once-off, not per month" with a disclosure ribbon. Keep it that way.

---

## 2. CONFIRM WITH YOUR ATTORNEY AND NAMFISA BEFORE PRINTING

2.1 **The default-interest figure.** The documents leave the default-interest rate as a blank drafted as "not more than 5%, for not more than three months". That 5%/3-month cap comes from NAMFISA consumer material, **not** from a confirmed reading of the ministerial determination. Confirm the current figure before you fill the blank.

2.2 **Every statute section number.** Because the primary sources could not be opened, section references (e.g. to the Microlending Act, the Usury Act 73 of 1968, the Magistrates' Court Act 32 of 1944, the Prescription Act 68 of 1969, the Credit Bureau Regulations) are drafted conservatively but **must be checked against the gazetted text** before the first print run.

2.3 **The cooling-off period.** Drafted as **three business days**. Confirm the exact count and whether it is business or calendar days.

2.4 **Submit the loan agreement to NAMFISA.** NAMFISA reviews and approves a microlender's loan-agreement form as part of registration, and publishes a standard form. Compare this agreement against theirs and submit it.

2.5 **The revenue stamp.** The Stamp Duties Act was amended in 2024. The agreement leaves a revenue-stamp box on the printed original but deliberately **prints no amount** — confirm the current duty with NAMRA.

2.6 **Data protection.** There is no Data Protection Act in force in Namibia, so the privacy notice is grounded in **contractual consent** and the statutory credit-check duty, not in a data-protection statute. Do not add a citation to a Namibian data-protection law.

2.7 **You must actually be subscribed to a registered credit bureau** and must actually complete and file a **written affordability assessment** for every loan. Several documents state that these were done; they must genuinely be done, not just recited.

---

## 3. CHANGES YOUR LEDGER APP NEEDS TO MATCH THIS PAPERWORK

The documents promise things the current app does not yet enforce. Flag these to whoever maintains the app:

3.1 **Cap validation.** Block or warn on save when `(interest + serviceFee) / principal` exceeds 0.30.

3.2 **Cumulative-charge ceiling.** Never let total finance charges on one loan exceed 30% of its principal, however many extensions occur.

3.3 **Early settlement should be pro rata.** The agreement gives the borrower a pro-rata settlement figure if they pay early; the app's flat, once-off interest does not reduce for early payment. Reconcile the two, or the paperwork over-promises.

3.4 **In duplum.** Interest and charges must stop once accrued unpaid interest equals the outstanding capital. The app should enforce this hard stop.

3.5 **Extension mechanism.** Rework rollovers away from "another full cycle" toward default interest (capped) or a documented new loan — see 1.3.

---

## 4. CROSS-DOCUMENT ITEMS TO RECONCILE

An independent three-way review (a consumer-advocate reading, an adversarial-attorney reading, and an operations reading against the app) flagged these to tidy up before use. None is a legal error on its own; each is an internal-consistency point:

- **The extension charge** is described one way in the pre-agreement quotation and another in the agreement — make them say the same thing once you have settled 1.3.
- **The payment-appropriation order** (which debt a payment clears first) is stated at different levels of detail across the agreement, the receipt, the statement and the arrears letter. Pick one order and use identical wording everywhere.
- **Annexure C** (an instalment schedule) is referred to but not included — add it or remove the reference.
- **NAMFISA's contact details** appear with slight differences between documents — set them once and reuse.
- Replace every remaining **[SQUARE-BRACKET]** placeholder before printing; never present a document for signature with a bracket still showing.

---

## 5. FILL-IN CHECKLIST — what only you can supply

Already filled in for you across the pack: **Quickserve Financial Services CC**, CC registration **CC/2026/01904**, and the phone/WhatsApp number **+264 81 264 6222**.

Still to fill in (left as highlighted blanks on purpose):

- NAMFISA microlender registration number and its expiry date — **leave blank until the certificate is issued; the pack deliberately makes no registration claim in the meantime**
- Physical street address, postal address, and email
- Principal officer's name
- Your confirmed interest rate and service fee (subject to the 30% cap in 1.2)
- The default-interest rate (subject to 2.1)
- Your record-retention period and maximum-extensions policy

---

## 6. THE DOCUMENTS IN THIS PACK

**Before the loan** — Loan Application Form · Pre-Agreement Statement & Quotation · Affordability Assessment Worksheet.
**The loan** — Microloan Agreement · Schedule of Fees & Charges (Annexure A) · Payment Receipt.
**When it is settled** — Paid-Up Letter / Settlement Confirmation.
**If it is not paid** — Final Letter of Demand · Acknowledgement of Debt & Payment Arrangement.
**Governance** — Consent & Privacy Notice · Debit Order / Payment Authority Mandate.

This is a focused, professional set. Some optional or internal-only forms (a statement of account, an early-settlement quotation, a first-reminder letter, a write-off notice, and a client-rights charter) are intentionally left out to keep the pack lean; they can be added back at any time. **No rollover / loan-extension form is included on purpose** — until the rollover pricing is confirmed lawful (clause 1.3), issuing paperwork for it would encourage a practice that is likely unlawful.

Each document is supplied as an editable Word file (for you to fill in and adjust) and as a print-ready PDF (what the client receives).

---

*Prepared as a drafting aid for Quickserve Financial Services CC. Not legal advice. Have a Namibian legal practitioner review the full pack before use.*

**Short-term (payday) microloan — a microlending transaction under the Microlending Act 7 of 2018**

This form is an application only. It is not a loan agreement and it does not oblige us to lend you money, or oblige you to borrow. Applying costs you nothing.

1.4 If you would like this form explained to you in another language, or read out to you, tell our officer before you start. We will do that free of charge.

16.1 **Credit bureau enquiry.** You give us permission to ask a credit bureau registered with the Bank of Namibia (for example Compuscan Credit Reference Bureau (Pty) Ltd or TransUnion Credit Bureau Namibia (Pty) Ltd) for your credit record, and to use that record to assess this application.

16.2 **Reporting to credit bureaus.** You give us permission to send information about your loan and your payment record to those credit bureaus. Where we report to a credit bureau, we report **both** the good and the bad. If you pay on time, that is what would be reported; if you fall behind, that would also be reported, and it can make it harder for you to borrow elsewhere.

16.3 **Employer verification.** You give us permission to contact the employer named in section 6 to confirm that you work there, your job, your staff number and your income. We will not discuss the amount of your loan or your debt with anyone at your workplace who is not part of that verification.

16.4 **Bank verification.** You give us permission to confirm with your bank that the account details in section 7 are correct.

16.5 **Collections.** If you fall behind and we have to hand your account to a debt collector or an attorney, you give us permission to give them the information they need to collect the debt. We will tell you in writing before we do that.

16.6 **Why we hold your information.** We collect and keep the information in this form to identify you, to assess whether you can afford the loan, to manage the loan if it is granted, to collect what is owed, and to keep the records we are required by law to keep.

16.7 **Who else sees it.** Apart from the people named above, we will not give your information to anyone else without your written permission, unless a law or a court order requires it.

16.8 **How long we keep it.** We keep your file for at least [RETENTION PERIOD — QUICKSERVE POLICY, IN YEARS] years after your loan is fully settled, or after this application is declined, and then we destroy it securely.

16.9 **Your rights.** You may ask us at any time what information we hold about you and what we have sent to a credit bureau. If anything is wrong, tell us and we will correct it and tell the bureau. You may also ask the credit bureau directly for your own credit report.

16.10 **Withdrawing consent.** You may withdraw this consent in writing at any time. Withdrawing it does not undo checks we already made, and does not cancel any loan agreement you have already signed with us.

17.1 We check your documents and, where we use a credit bureau, carry out a credit-bureau enquiry.

17.3 If we can help you, we give you a written **Pre-Agreement Statement and Quotation**. It shows, in Namibian Dollars and cents, exactly how much cash you get, how much the loan costs, the total you must repay, and the date you must repay it.

17.4 You may take that quotation away, think about it, and compare it with other lenders. You owe us nothing for it and you are not bound by it.

17.5 Only if you accept the quotation do we prepare the loan agreement. We explain it to you, you read it or we read it to you, and both of us sign it. You get a free copy of the signed agreement before or at the moment we pay you the money.

17.6 We may decline your application. If we do, we will tell you the main reason.

17.7 Applying costs you nothing. We charge no application fee, no assessment fee and no fee for a quotation.

# PRE-AGREEMENT STATEMENT AND QUOTATION

**Quotation number:** [QUOTATION NO.]  **Date issued:** [DD / MM / YYYY]  **Valid until:** [DD / MM / YYYY]

**This is not a loan agreement. You are not bound by anything in this document.**

---

## 1. WHAT THIS DOCUMENT IS

1.1 This document tells you, before you commit to anything, exactly what the loan we are offering you will cost.

1.2 The law requires us to give you this in writing before you sign a loan agreement. We give it to you free of charge.

1.3 Take it away. Think about it. Show it to someone you trust. Compare it with what other registered lenders offer you. You owe us nothing and you may simply not come back.

1.4 If you do decide to go ahead, we will then prepare a loan agreement on exactly these terms. Nothing in the agreement will cost you more than the figures in this quotation.

1.5 If anything in this document is unclear, ask us before you sign anything. We will explain it in a language you understand, and we will read it to you if you prefer.

---

## 2. WHO THIS QUOTATION IS FOR

| Item | Detail |
| --- | --- |
| Applicant full name | [FULL NAME] |
| Namibian ID number | [ID NUMBER] |
| Mobile number | [+264 ____ ______] |
| Physical address | [STREET ADDRESS, TOWN] |
| Related application number | [APPLICATION NO.] |
| Prepared by (officer) | [OFFICER FULL NAME] |

---

## 3. THE LOAN WE ARE OFFERING YOU

| Item | Detail |
| --- | --- |
| Type of loan | Short-term (payday) microloan |
| Repaid in | **One single payment** on the due date |
| Number of repayments | 1 |
| Date we would pay you the cash (issue date) | [DD / MM / YYYY] |
| Date you must repay (due date) | [DD / MM / YYYY] |
| Number of days the loan runs | [NUMBER] days |
| How we would pay you | [CASH / BANK TRANSFER TO YOUR ACCOUNT] |
| How you would repay us | [CASH AT OUR OFFICE / BANK TRANSFER (EFT) / DEBIT ORDER] |

---

## 4. WHAT THIS LOAN WILL COST YOU

All amounts are in Namibian Dollars and cents.

| Line | Description | Amount (N$) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **A** | **Principal debt — the cash amount we pay you** | **[N$ ______ . ____]** |
| B | Interest for the whole loan term — a once-off charge of [RATE]% of line A | [N$ ______ . ____] |
| C | Service fee — a once-off flat fee | [N$ ______ . ____] |
| **D** | **TOTAL FINANCE CHARGES (B + C) — everything you pay us above the cash you receive** | **[N$ ______ . ____]** |
| **E** | **TOTAL AMOUNT YOU MUST REPAY (A + D)** | **[N$ ______ . ____]** |
| **F** | **AMOUNT OF YOUR SINGLE REPAYMENT, DUE ON [DD / MM / YYYY]** | **[N$ ______ . ____]** |

**In plain words:** we pay you **[N$ ______ . ____]** on [DD / MM / YYYY], and on [DD / MM / YYYY] you pay us back **[N$ ______ . ____]** in one payment. The loan costs you **[N$ ______ . ____]**.

---

## 5. THE PARTS THAT MAKE UP THE COST

5.1 There are exactly two charges, and both are shown separately in the table above:

- **Interest** (line B) — a once-off charge worked out as a percentage of the cash you receive.
- **Service fee** (line C) — a once-off flat amount for opening and administering the loan.

5.2 **There are no other charges.** No application fee. No assessment fee. No fee for this quotation. No disbursement fee. No monthly admin fee. No insurance premium.

5.3 **Both charges are once-off charges for the whole term of this loan. Neither is charged per month.** If your loan runs for 30 days, you pay lines B and C once. They do not repeat.

5.4 Interest is **flat and simple**. It is worked out once on the cash amount you receive. It does not compound and it is not recalculated each month.

---

## 6. THE LEGAL LIMIT ON WHAT WE MAY CHARGE

6.1 Namibian law sets a maximum on the **total** of everything a microlender may charge a borrower above the cash advanced. That maximum covers the interest **and** the service fee **and** any other charge, added together.

6.2 For a short-term microloan repayable within five months, that maximum is **30% of the principal debt, once off** — not 30% per month.

6.3 Here is how this loan measures against that limit:

| Check | Figure |
| --- | --- |
| Total finance charges (line D) | [N$ ______ . ____] |
| Principal debt (line A) | [N$ ______ . ____] |
| Total finance charges as a percentage of the principal (D ÷ A × 100) | [____] % |
| Maximum permitted for this type of loan | 30% |
| Is this loan within the maximum? | [YES — this must be YES; if it is not, we may not offer you this loan] |

6.4 We will never ask you for, or accept, more than the maximum the law allows. If it ever turned out that we had charged you more, the excess would not be owing, and anything you had already paid over the limit would be refunded to you.

---

## 7. FIGURES FOR COMPARING US WITH OTHER LENDERS

Use these when you shop around. Ask every other lender for the same three figures.

| Comparison figure | This loan |
| --- | --- |
| Cost for every N$100 you borrow | [N$ ______ . ____] |
| Total cost as a percentage of the amount borrowed, for the whole term | [____] % over [NUMBER] days |
| The same cost expressed as a yearly rate, **for comparison only** — this is not what we charge you, because your loan does not run for a year | [____] % per year |

The yearly figure looks large because the loan is short. It is included so you can compare a 30-day loan against a lender quoting a yearly rate. **What you actually pay is line E in section 4, and nothing more.**

---

## 8. HOW AND WHEN YOU REPAY

8.1 You repay in **one payment** of **[N$ ______ . ____]** on **[DD / MM / YYYY]**.

8.2 You may pay in cash at our office, or by bank transfer, or by debit order if you have signed a debit order authority. Always keep your receipt or proof of payment.

8.3 Our banking details for repayment are: [BANK NAME], account name [ACCOUNT NAME], account number [ACCOUNT NUMBER], branch code [BRANCH CODE]. Use your ID number as the payment reference.

8.4 If you sign a debit order authority, cancelling it later does not cancel the loan. You would still owe the money.

8.5 You may ask us at any time for a statement showing every charge we have raised, every payment you have made, and what is still outstanding. The first statement, and the statement we give you when the loan is settled, are free. If you ask for a duplicate copy of a statement, we may charge no more than **N$2.00 per page**.

---

## 9. HOW WE APPLY EVERY PAYMENT YOU MAKE

**Read this clause carefully. It affects how quickly your debt goes down.**

9.1 Every payment you make is applied in this order:

- **first**, to any legal costs or collection charges properly incurred (if there are any);
- **then**, to the service fee;
- **then**, to interest, including any default interest;
- **and only what is left over** reduces the principal — the cash amount you were paid.

9.2 This order applies even if you write something different on the deposit slip or tell us to apply the money differently.

9.3 **Worked example — these are not your figures, they are only to show you how it works.**

| Step | Amount (N$) |
| --- | --- |
| Cash paid to the borrower (principal) | 1 000.00 |
| Interest, once off | 200.00 |
| Service fee, once off | 100.00 |
| Total finance charges | 300.00 |
| Total repayable | 1 300.00 |

The borrower pays **N$500.00** on the due date. That N$500.00 is applied like this:

| Applied to | Amount (N$) | Left owing on that item |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Service fee | 100.00 | 0.00 |
| Interest | 200.00 | 0.00 |
| Principal | 200.00 | 800.00 |
| **Total applied** | **500.00** | **Balance outstanding: 800.00** |

So after paying N$500.00, the borrower still owes **N$800.00** of principal. The charges were cleared first.

9.4 This is why paying the full amount on the due date is always cheaper for you than paying part of it.

---

## 10. IF YOU PAY EARLY

10.1 You may pay the loan off early, at any time, in one payment or several, and **we will not charge you any penalty or fee for doing so**.

10.2 If you settle early, you do **not** pay the full finance charges shown in line D. You pay the finance charges **only for the days you actually had the money** — worked out in proportion to the term of the loan.

10.3 **Worked example — not your figures.** On the example loan in clause 9.3, the finance charges of N$300.00 are for a 30-day term, which is N$10.00 a day. A borrower who settles on day 12 pays the N$1 000.00 principal plus 12 days of charges (N$120.00) — that is N$1 120.00, not N$1 300.00.

10.4 Ask us for a settlement figure before you pay early, and we will work it out for you in writing, free of charge.

---

## 11. IF YOU CHANGE YOUR MIND AFTER SIGNING

11.1 If you sign the loan agreement and then change your mind, you may cancel it within **three (3) business days** after you signed.

11.2 To cancel, tell us in writing (a WhatsApp message or letter to us is enough) and pay back the full cash amount we gave you at the same time.

11.3 If you cancel this way, you pay finance charges **only for the days you actually had the money**, not for the full term. There is no cancellation penalty.

11.4 Business days do not include Saturdays, Sundays or Namibian public holidays.

---

## 12. IF YOU DO NOT PAY ON THE DUE DATE

We would rather help you than penalise you. Call us on +264 81 264 6222 **before** the due date if you know you will have a problem.

12.1 If you do not pay on the due date, we may charge **default interest of not more than 5% of the outstanding amount that is in default, for each month it stays unpaid, for a maximum of three months — or such lower maximum as Namibian law may set, whichever is less**. After three months no further default interest may be charged.

12.2 Default interest is the **only** extra charge for late payment. We do not charge a second round of the interest or service fee in line B or C.

12.3 **The *in duplum* rule protects you.** *In duplum* is a rule of Namibian law which means, in plain words: **the unpaid interest and charges on your loan can never grow to more than the capital you still owe.** Once the unpaid interest and charges reach that level, they stop growing. We apply this rule to your account automatically.

12.4 Before we hand your account to a debt collector or an attorney, we will tell you in writing that we intend to do so, and give you a chance to pay or make an arrangement.

12.5 Before we start court proceedings, we will send you a written demand first.

12.6 If we have to enforce the debt in court, you may become liable for our legal costs and collection charges. Those costs are always subject to being assessed and allowed by the court or the taxing master — we cannot simply name a figure.

12.7 Where we report to a credit bureau, we report your payment record — the good as well as the bad.

12.8 We will never threaten you, shame you, take your property, or take your bank card, PIN or original ID.

---

## 13. IF YOU NEED MORE TIME (EXTENSION)

13.1 If you cannot pay on the due date, you may ask us to extend the due date. We do not have to agree.

13.2 If we do agree, the change must be put in **writing and signed by both you and us** on a separate extension form. An extension that is only recorded in our system, or only agreed over the phone or on WhatsApp, is not valid and does not bind you.

13.3 Before you sign any extension, we will show you in writing exactly what the extension costs and what your new total repayable is.

13.4 **An extension can never push the total finance charges on this loan above the legal maximum described in section 6.** Whatever is agreed on an extension, the total of everything you pay us above the cash you received stays within that ceiling.

---

## 14. WHAT THIS LOAN DOES NOT INVOLVE

14.1 **No compulsory insurance.** We do not require you to take out any insurance policy to get this loan, and this quotation contains no insurance premium.

14.2 **No card, no PIN, no originals.** We do not take or keep your bank card, your PIN, or your original ID, passport or driver's licence, as security or for collection. The law forbids it.

14.3 **No blank documents.** We will never ask you to sign a blank or incomplete document. Every figure and every date will be filled in before you sign.

14.4 **No salary deduction unless you separately agree.** We will not arrange any deduction from your salary unless you sign a separate written authority for it, and only if that is lawfully available at the time.

---

## 15. HOW LONG THIS QUOTATION LASTS

15.1 This quotation is valid until **[DD / MM / YYYY]** — that is [NUMBER] days from the date it was issued.

15.2 Until that date, if you come back and accept it, and your circumstances have not materially changed, we will lend on exactly these terms and at exactly these figures.

15.3 After that date the figures fall away, and we would need to reassess your application, because your income, your other debts or the applicable maximum charges may have changed.

15.4 We may withdraw this quotation before that date only if we discover that information given to us was untrue or incomplete, or if something happens that materially changes your ability to repay. If we withdraw it, we will tell you why.

15.5 **You owe us nothing for this quotation and you are under no obligation to accept it.**

---

## 16. IF YOU ARE NOT HAPPY WITH US

16.1 Speak to the officer who assisted you first. If that does not resolve it, put your complaint in writing to the Principal Officer of QuickServe Cashloan at the address and email on this letterhead, or on +264 81 264 6222.

16.2 We will acknowledge your written complaint and respond to it.

16.3 If you are still not satisfied, you may take the matter to **NAMFISA**, which supervises microlenders in Namibia:

16.4 You may ask us for a NAMFISA complaint intake form and we will give you one, free of charge. We also keep a copy of the Microlending Act, the regulations and the NAMFISA standards, and our own complaints procedure, available for you to read on request.

---

## 17. ACKNOWLEDGEMENT BY THE APPLICANT

I, the person who signs below, confirm that:

17.1 I received this Pre-Agreement Statement and Quotation, free of charge, **before** I was asked to sign any loan agreement.

# MICROLOAN AGREEMENT

**Short-term microlending transaction under the Microlending Act 7 of 2018 (Namibia)**

| Reference | Detail |
|---|---|
| Agreement number | [AGREEMENT NUMBER] |
| Loan number in our loan book | [LOAN NUMBER] |

| Copy | [ ] Borrower's original  [ ] Lender's original |

**Please read this before you sign.** This agreement is written in plain English on purpose. If any part of it is unclear, stop and ask us. We must explain it to you in a language you understand, and you may ask for it to be read out to you. You may take it away and read it before you sign. Nothing in this document may be signed while it is blank or incomplete.

---

## 1. WHO THIS AGREEMENT IS BETWEEN

1.1 **The Lender ("we", "us", "our")**

1.3 **Your work and income**

| Item | Detail |

| Employer name | [EMPLOYER NAME] |
| Your job title | [JOB TITLE] |
| Staff / payroll number | [STAFF OR PAYROLL NUMBER] |

1.4 **Your next of kin.** This is a person we may contact only if we cannot reach you at any of the numbers above. We will not discuss your loan, your balance or your arrears with this person.

1.5 **What this loan is.** This is a microlending transaction as defined in the Microlending Act 7 of 2018. It is a short-term loan of not more than N$100,000.00 which must be repaid, together with all finance charges, within five (5) months of the issue date. Because of that short term, the legal maximum for total finance charges set out in clause 3.5 applies to it.

1.6 **What the loan is for.** [PURPOSE OF LOAN].

---

## 2. THE MONEY — WHAT YOU GET AND WHAT YOU PAY

2.1 **The complete cost of your loan.** The table below is the full cost of this loan when you repay on time. If you pay the amount in row F by the due date, there is nothing further to pay. The only other amounts that can ever arise are: default interest and legal costs, and then only if you do not pay (clause 9); and the small items listed in the Schedule of Fees and Charges (Annexure A), such as a fee for a duplicate copy of a statement. **We will never charge you anything that is not provided for in this agreement or in Annexure A.** If a charge is not written down in one of those places, you do not owe it.

| # | Item | Amount |
|---|---|---|
| A | **Principal debt — the cash we hand to you** | **N$[PRINCIPAL]** |
| B | Interest at [INTEREST RATE]% of the principal, charged once for the whole loan period | N$[INTEREST AMOUNT] |
| C | Service fee (a flat, once-off amount) | N$[SERVICE FEE] |
| D | **Total finance charges (B + C) — everything you pay us above the cash you received** | **N$[TOTAL FINANCE CHARGES]** |
| E | Total finance charges as a percentage of the principal (D ÷ A) — **must not be more than 30%** | [TOTAL FINANCE CHARGE PERCENTAGE]% |
| F | **TOTAL AMOUNT REPAYABLE (A + D)** | **N$[TOTAL AMOUNT REPAYABLE]** |

2.2 **The total amount repayable in words:** [TOTAL AMOUNT REPAYABLE IN WORDS] Namibian Dollars and [CENTS IN WORDS] cents.

2.3 **Dates and repayments**

| Item | Detail |
|---|---|
| Issue date (the day the cash is paid to you) | [ISSUE DATE] |
| Due date (the day the full amount must be in our hands) | [DUE DATE] |
| Loan period | [NUMBER OF DAYS] days |
| Number of repayments | 1 (one) |
| Amount of that one repayment | **N$[TOTAL AMOUNT REPAYABLE]** |
| How the cash is paid to you | [CASH / EFT / E-WALLET] |

2.4 This loan is repaid in **one single payment** on the due date. If we ever agree that you may pay in instalments, that arrangement is only valid if it is written down and signed by both of us on an instalment schedule attached to this agreement as Annexure C.

2.5 **Comparison figure only.** Expressed as a simple annual rate for comparison with other credit, the finance charges on this loan work out to [ANNUAL FINANCE CHARGE RATE]% per year, calculated as (D ÷ A) × (365 ÷ loan period in days). **This is only a comparison figure to help you shop around. It is not an extra charge, it is not what you pay, and it does not mean we charge interest each year.** What you actually pay is the single figure in row F, once, for this loan.

2.6 **No compulsory insurance.** We have not required you to take out any insurance to get this loan, and we may not do so. If you have chosen any insurance in connection with this loan, it is listed here and you will be given a free copy of the policy: [INSURANCE — WRITE "NONE" IF THERE IS NONE].

---

## 3. HOW THE INTEREST AND THE SERVICE FEE WORK

3.1 **The interest is a flat, once-off charge.** The interest is a fixed percentage of the principal in row A. It is calculated once, at the start, for the whole loan period. It is **not** charged per month, it is **not** charged per week, and it does **not** compound. Compounding means charging interest on interest — that does not happen here.

3.2 Because it is calculated once and does not compound, the interest amount in row B does not grow while the loan runs to its due date. Whether you pay on day 5 or day 30, the interest shown in row B is the most you can ever be charged for this loan period. If you pay early you pay **less** than row B — see clause 7.

3.3 **Worked example.** These are example figures, not your figures. Your figures are in the table in clause 2.

| Item | Example |
|---|---|
| Principal | N$1,000.00 |
| Interest at 25% of the principal, once-off | N$250.00 |
| Service fee, flat | N$50.00 |
| **Total finance charges** | **N$300.00 (30% of the principal)** |
| **Total repayable on the due date** | **N$1,300.00** |

If the loan runs from 1 March to 31 March, the borrower receives N$1,000.00 on 1 March and pays N$1,300.00 on 31 March. The N$300.00 does not increase during March.

3.4 **The service fee is part of your finance charges.** Namibian law treats every amount you owe us that is not the principal as a "finance charge". The service fee is therefore counted **inside** the legal maximum in clause 3.5 — never on top of it.

3.5 **The legal ceiling on what we may charge you.** The total of all finance charges under this agreement — interest, the service fee, any charge added when the due date is extended under clause 8, and any other amount you owe us that is not principal — **will never exceed 30% of the principal debt in row A**, this being the maximum finance charge rate determined by the Registrar under the Usury Act 73 of 1968 for a microlending transaction repayable within five months.

3.6 **Protective clause.** We will not stipulate for, demand or receive any amount that exceeds the maximum finance charge permitted by law at the time. If any figure in this agreement, or any figure we later charge, turns out to exceed that maximum, then:

(a) the excess is void and you do not owe it;

(b) the lawful maximum applies automatically in its place, without either of us having to sign anything; and

(c) if you have already paid the excess, we will refund it to you within 10 business days of it being identified.

3.7 Default interest under clause 9.3 is dealt with separately and has its own legal ceiling.

---

## 4. HOW YOU REPAY US

4.1 **When.** The full amount in row F must be in our hands on or before **[DUE DATE]**. Paying on the due date itself is on time. Paying the day after is late.

4.2 **How.** You may pay by any of these methods:

(a) **Bank transfer / EFT** into: [BANK NAME], account name [ACCOUNT NAME], account number [ACCOUNT NUMBER], branch code [BRANCH CODE]. Use **[REFERENCE — YOUR NAME AND LOAN NUMBER]** as the payment reference.

(b) **Cash**, in person at our office at [PHYSICAL STREET ADDRESS], during office hours. We will give you a written receipt on the spot. Never pay cash to anyone without getting a receipt.

(c) **Debit order**, but only if you have signed a separate debit order mandate. See clause 4.6.

4.3 **Do not pay in any other way.** Do not pay into a personal account, do not hand cash to a person at your workplace, and do not send money to any number other than the one on this agreement. If someone asks you to, refuse and phone us on +264 81 264 6222.

4.4 **Keep your proof of payment.** Keep the bank transfer confirmation, the deposit slip, the e-wallet confirmation SMS or the receipt we gave you, **until you have our paid-up letter**. If there is ever a dispute about whether you paid, your proof of payment settles it. Please also send a copy of the proof to us on WhatsApp at +264 81 264 6222 on the day you pay, so we can update the loan book immediately.

4.5 **When a payment counts.** A payment counts on the date the money actually reaches our account or our hands. A transfer sent after banking hours, or over a weekend or public holiday, may only reach us on the next business day. Please allow for that.

4.6 **Debit order.** Any debit order is set up on a separate signed mandate, through a payment system registered with the Bank of Namibia. If you cancel the debit order, **the debt does not disappear** — cancelling the mandate cancels only the automatic collection, not this agreement, and you must then pay by another method in clause 4.2.

4.7 **No salary deduction unless you sign for it separately.** We will not ask your employer to deduct anything from your salary unless you have signed a separate written authority for that, on a separate form. Under the Labour Act 11 of 2007 your employer may not make deductions you have not agreed to in writing, and deductions you have agreed to may not add up to more than one third of your pay.

4.8 **Overpayment.** If you pay us more than you owe, we will refund the difference to your bank account within 5 business days of you asking, or immediately on final settlement, at no charge.

---

## 5. HOW WE APPLY THE MONEY YOU PAY — PLEASE READ THIS CLAUSE CAREFULLY

5.1 **The order.** Every payment we receive is applied in this order:

(a) **first**, to any legal costs and collection charges actually incurred (only if clause 9.6 applies);

(b) **then**, to the service fee;

(c) **then**, to interest, including any default interest;

(d) **and only what is left over reduces the principal.**

5.2 This order applies to every payment, whatever you write on the deposit slip or in a message, and whether or not you tell us to apply it differently. This is agreed between us and it overrides any contrary instruction or note. It does not reduce your rights on cancellation (clause 6) or on early settlement (clause 7), where only pro rata charges apply.

5.3 **Why this matters to you.** It means that a part payment made early in the loan goes mostly towards the charges and barely reduces the cash amount you borrowed. **Do not be surprised when a part payment leaves the balance looking high.** The example below shows exactly how it works.

5.4 **Worked example.** Using the example loan in clause 3.3 — principal N$1,000.00, finance charges N$300.00, total repayable N$1,300.00 — the borrower pays N$400.00 on 15 March.

| Step | Applied to | Amount | What is left |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Legal / collection costs | N$0.00 | — |
| 2 | Service fee | N$50.00 | Service fee now N$0.00 |
| 3 | Interest | N$250.00 | Interest now N$0.00 |
| 4 | Principal | N$100.00 | Principal now N$900.00 |
| | **Balance still owing after the N$400.00 payment** | | **N$900.00** |

So a payment of N$400.00 reduced the cash borrowed by only N$100.00. The other N$300.00 cleared the charges. This is normal and it is what clause 5.1 means.

5.5 The good news in the same example: once the charges are cleared, every further N$1.00 you pay reduces the principal by a full N$1.00, because there is nothing else left for a payment to go to.

5.6 You may ask us at any time, free of charge, for a written breakdown showing exactly how each of your payments was applied. See clause 14.2.

---

## 6. YOUR RIGHT TO CANCEL — THE FIRST THREE BUSINESS DAYS

6.1 **You may cancel this agreement within three (3) business days after you sign it.** You do not have to give us a reason. This is your right under the Microlending Act 7 of 2018 and we cannot take it away.

6.2 To cancel, tell us in writing — a WhatsApp message, an email, or a signed note handed in at our office is enough — and **at the same time repay the cash we gave you**.

6.3 If you cancel this way, you pay finance charges **only for the days you actually had the money**, not for the full loan period. There is no cancellation fee and no penalty.

6.4 **Worked example.** Using the example loan in clause 3.3: the borrower signs and receives N$1,000.00 on 1 March and cancels on 3 March, having had the money for 2 days of a 30-day loan.

| Item | Calculation | Amount |
|---|---|---|
| Principal to be repaid | — | N$1,000.00 |
| Finance charges for 2 days | N$300.00 × 2 ÷ 30 | N$20.00 |
| **Total to repay on cancellation** | | **N$1,020.00** |

6.5 "Business day" means any day other than a Saturday, a Sunday or an official Namibian public holiday.

6.6 Cancelling under this clause is not the same as settling early (clause 7) and it is not a default (clause 9). Nothing negative is reported to a credit bureau because you used this right.

---

## 7. PAYING EARLY — YOUR RIGHT TO SETTLE BEFORE THE DUE DATE

7.1 **You may pay this loan off early, at any time, in one payment or in several.** You may also pay extra at any time. We may not charge you any penalty, fee or additional amount for doing so, and we will not.

7.2 **You pay finance charges only for the days you actually had the money.** When you settle early, the finance charges are reduced in proportion to the number of days that have passed.

7.3 **The settlement figure is worked out like this:**

> **Settlement figure = principal still outstanding + (total finance charges × days elapsed ÷ total days of the loan) − finance charges you have already paid**

where "days elapsed" is counted from the issue date to the day you settle.

7.4 **Worked example.** Using the example loan in clause 3.3 — N$1,000.00 principal, N$300.00 finance charges, 30-day loan — the borrower has paid nothing and settles on day 10.

| Item | Calculation | Amount |
|---|---|---|
| Principal outstanding | — | N$1,000.00 |
| Finance charges for 10 days | N$300.00 × 10 ÷ 30 | N$100.00 |
| Less finance charges already paid | — | N$0.00 |
| **Settlement figure on day 10** | | **N$1,100.00** |

The borrower saves N$200.00 by settling on day 10 instead of day 30.

7.5 **Ask us for the figure first.** Phone or WhatsApp us on +264 81 264 6222 and we will give you a written settlement quote, **free of charge**, valid for the date stated on it. Pay the exact quoted figure on or before that date and the loan is settled in full.

7.6 Once you have settled in full we will, without you having to ask and at no cost, give you a paid-up letter, cancel any debit order mandate, and — where we have reported this loan to a credit bureau — update your record with that bureau. See clause 14.3.

---

## 8. EXTENDING THE DUE DATE (A "ROLLOVER")

8.1 **What an extension is.** If you cannot pay on the due date, you may ask us to move the due date to a later date. This is called an extension or a rollover.

8.2 **No new money changes hands.** An extension is not a new loan. We do not pay you anything further and you do not receive any further cash. It is a change to this same loan: the due date moves out, and the amount you owe stays owing.

8.3 **An extension is only valid if it is in writing and signed by both of us.** We will complete an **Extension Agreement** form which sets out, in Namibian Dollars and cents: the balance outstanding on the day of the extension, the additional finance charge (if any), the new total repayable, and the new due date. You sign it, we sign it, and you get a free copy. **An extension recorded only in our app, or agreed only by phone or WhatsApp, is not valid and does not bind you.** Namibian law does not permit us to increase what you owe without your written signature.

8.4 **What an extension may cost you.** An extension may carry a further finance charge on the principal still outstanding, calculated at the rate in clause 2. **But that further charge is subject to the ceiling in clause 3.5.** The 30% ceiling applies to this loan as a whole, once — not to each cycle separately. So the most we may ever add on an extension is whatever room is left under the ceiling, and **that may be nothing at all**.

8.5 **Worked examples of clause 8.4.**

| Situation | Finance charges already charged | Ceiling (30% of N$1,000.00 principal) | Most that may be added on extension |
|---|---|---|---|
| Loan already charged the full 30% | N$300.00 | N$300.00 | **N$0.00 — nothing further may be charged** |
| Loan charged 20% | N$200.00 | N$300.00 | **N$100.00, and never more** |
| Loan charged 15% | N$150.00 | N$300.00 | **N$150.00, and never more** |

8.6 **WARNING — please take this seriously.** Extending a loan repeatedly is expensive and it is how a small loan becomes a long problem. Every extension pushes the date out without reducing what you borrowed, and because of clause 5.1 your payments clear charges before they touch the principal. If you find yourself asking for a second extension, that is a sign the loan is not affordable. **Talk to us instead about a written payment arrangement that actually reduces the principal.** We would rather agree a realistic plan with you than roll a loan over again.

8.7 **Limits on extensions.**

(a) The due date may not be extended beyond **five (5) months from the issue date** in clause 2.3. That is a legal boundary for this kind of loan, not a policy of ours.

(b) The maximum number of extensions on this loan is **[MAXIMUM NUMBER OF EXTENSIONS]**.

(c) We are not obliged to grant an extension, and you are never obliged to ask for one. Asking and being refused is not a default.

8.8 **An extension is an acknowledgement of the debt.** When you sign an Extension Agreement you confirm the balance stated in it. Please check that balance before you sign, and ask for a statement of account if you want to see how it was calculated.

---

## 9. IF YOU DO NOT PAY (DEFAULT)

9.1 **What counts as default.** You are in default if:

(a) the total amount repayable is not paid in full by the due date, and no extension has been signed under clause 8; or

(b) you gave us information in your application that you knew was false and that would have changed our decision to lend; or

(c) a court sequestrates your estate or you are placed under administration.

Being a day or two late because a transfer took time to clear is not what this clause is aimed at. Contact us and we will sort it out.

9.2 **What we will do, in order.**

(a) We will contact you by phone, SMS, WhatsApp or email to find out what has happened and to offer you a payment arrangement.

(b) If that does not resolve it, we will send you a **written letter of demand** to your address in clause 1.2, setting out exactly what is owed — principal, interest, service fee and any default interest, separately — and giving you a clear deadline of not less than [DEMAND PERIOD — AT LEAST 7] business days to pay or to make an arrangement.

(c) Only if that deadline passes will we consider handing the account over, and we will tell you in writing before we do so (clause 9.5).

9.3 **Default interest.** From the day after the due date we may charge default interest on the amount outstanding at **[DEFAULT INTEREST RATE — NOT MORE THAN 5]% per month**, for a maximum of **three (3) months**. After three months no further default interest may be charged at all, and none will be.

(a) Default interest is subject to the same protective rule as clause 3.6: we will not charge more than the maximum permitted by law, and if the legal maximum is lower than the figure written above, the lower figure applies automatically and any excess is void and refundable.

(b) Default interest is charged on the amount actually outstanding, and it stops the moment you pay.

9.4 **The *in duplum* rule — a limit that protects you.** *In duplum* is a rule of Namibian law which means, in plain words: **unpaid interest and charges can never grow to more than the capital you still owe.** Once the interest and charges that have built up and remain unpaid equal the amount of principal still outstanding, they stop running completely. They do not start again until you make a payment that brings them back below that level. We apply this rule in your favour and we will not charge past it.

9.5 **Before we hand your account to anyone else.** We will not hand your account to a debt collector or to an attorney, and we will not start legal proceedings against you, without first telling you in writing that we intend to do so. That notice will be sent to your address in clause 1.2 and will tell you the amount owing and how long you have to prevent it.

9.6 **Legal costs.** If we do have to enforce this agreement through an attorney or a court, you are liable for the legal costs we actually incur, on the attorney-and-own-client scale, together with collection commission, tracing fees and disbursements. **Those costs are always subject to assessment by the court or the taxing master** — meaning a court may reduce them, and we may only recover what a court allows. We will not add a cost to your balance that we have not actually incurred, and every such cost will be itemised on your statement.

9.7 **Credit bureau.** If you default, we may report that to a registered credit bureau. This can make it harder and more expensive for you to borrow elsewhere. If you then settle, we will report the settlement too — see clause 13.

9.8 **What we will never do.** Whatever happens with your account, we will not:

(a) threaten you, shout at you, insult you or shame you;

(b) discuss your loan in any group chat, or with your colleagues, your family or your neighbours;

(c) come to your workplace to demand money, or send anyone to do so;

(d) take or hold any of your property;

(e) hold your bank card, your PIN, or any original document of yours — see clause 11;

(f) use any collection method that the law does not allow.

If anyone acting in our name does any of these things, report it to our principal officer and to NAMFISA under clause 15.

9.9 **Please talk to us.** If you know in advance that you will not be able to pay on the due date, tell us before the due date. A written payment arrangement costs you far less than a default. We will always consider one in good faith.

---

## 10. IF WE WRITE THE BALANCE OFF INTERNALLY

10.1 If a balance stays unpaid for a long time, we may mark it in our books as **written off**. That is an accounting decision inside our business about how we report our own figures.

10.2 **A write-off does not cancel your debt.** You still owe the money, we may still collect it, and we must still give you the notices in clause 9.5. We will not tell you a debt is cancelled unless it truly is.

10.3 If we ever do agree to cancel or reduce your debt, we will say so in a signed letter that states plainly that the balance is waived and that we will make no further claim. Only such a letter cancels a debt.

---

## 11. WHAT WE DO NOT TAKE FROM YOU

11.1 **We do not take or hold your bank card, your PIN, or your original documents.** We will never keep, or make use of, your bank card, your PIN or any banking password, your original Namibian identity document, your original passport or your original driver's licence — not as security, and not to help us collect. **This is prohibited by section 23(1)(f) of the Microlending Act 7 of 2018.**

11.2 **Copies only.** We take a copy of your Namibian ID, your latest payslip and your three months' bank statements because the law requires us to assess whether you can afford this loan. We look at your originals in front of you and hand them straight back. Nothing of yours is held in our safe.

11.3 **No blank or incomplete documents.** We may not ask you to sign anything that is blank or incomplete, and we have not. Every figure, date and name on this agreement was filled in before it was put in front of you. If any document we ever give you to sign has an empty space in it, **do not sign it** — hand it back and tell us.

11.4 **No pre-signed consent to judgment.** This agreement contains no consent to judgment and no acknowledgement of debt signed in advance. If a dispute ever arises, any such document would be a separate document, signed at that time, after a written demand.

11.5 **Report it.** If any person — including anyone claiming to work for us — asks you for your bank card, your PIN, an original document, or a signature on a blank form, refuse. Then report it to our principal officer and to NAMFISA on **0800 290 500**.

---

## 12. YOUR DECLARATION THAT YOU CAN AFFORD THIS LOAN

12.1 By signing this agreement you confirm that:

(a) everything you told us in your application is true and complete;

(b) you have told us about **all** your other debts, including any other cash loans, store accounts, hire purchase agreements and money owed to family or friends;

(c) you have told us about all deductions already coming off your salary;

(d) the payslip and bank statements you gave us are genuine and are your own;

(e) as far as you know, you are not about to be retrenched, suspended or dismissed, and your estate is not under sequestration or administration; and

(f) after paying this loan on the due date you will still be able to meet your ordinary living expenses and your other commitments.

12.2 **We did an affordability assessment.** Before granting this loan we assessed your income, your existing commitments and your disposable income, and, where we use a credit bureau, we performed a credit check through a registered credit bureau. We went through the assessment with you. A copy of that assessment is on your file and you may ask for a copy of it at any time, free of charge.

12.3 **Tell us if things change.** If your income drops, you change jobs, you lose your job, or your contact details change, tell us as soon as you can. It is much easier to arrange something before a payment is missed than afterwards.

12.4 If it turns out that you deliberately gave us false information to obtain this loan, that is a default under clause 9.1(b), and it may also be a criminal offence. Honest mistakes are not what this clause is about.

---

## 13. YOUR INFORMATION, CREDIT CHECKS AND CONSENT

13.1 **Credit bureau enquiry — required by law.** You consent to us obtaining a credit report on you from a registered credit bureau before we grant this loan, and at any time while any amount remains owing. Namibian law obliges us to do this; we may not lend to you without it.

13.2 **Reporting your account.** You consent to us giving registered credit bureaus information about this loan and how you pay it. This includes **good** payment behaviour as well as missed payments. If you pay well, that helps your record.

13.3 **Which bureaus.** Where we use a credit bureau, it is: [CREDIT BUREAU NAME(S) — FOR EXAMPLE COMPUSCAN CREDIT REFERENCE BUREAU (PTY) LTD AND/OR TRANSUNION CREDIT BUREAU NAMIBIA (PTY) LTD].

13.4 **What we hold and why.** We keep your name, ID number, contact details, employment and income information, bank details, your ID copy, payslip and bank statements, your affordability assessment, this agreement and your payment history. We use them only to assess your application, to administer and collect this loan, to meet our legal and regulatory duties, and to keep proper accounting records.

13.5 **Who we may share them with.** Only: registered credit bureaus (clause 13.3); our auditor, accounting officer or bookkeeper; NAMFISA and any other regulator or court that is legally entitled to them; and, if your account is handed over after the notice in clause 9.5, a debt collector or attorney. **We will not disclose your information to anyone else without your express consent.** This reflects the confidentiality duty in section 27 of the Microlending Act 7 of 2018.

13.6 **Your employer.** You separately consent to us contacting the employer named in clause 1.3 **for the limited purpose of verifying your employment and your income** before the loan is granted. We will not discuss your loan, your balance or your arrears with your employer without your further written consent.

13.7 **How long we keep your information.** We keep your loan file for [RETENTION PERIOD] years after the loan is finally settled, and then destroy it securely, unless a law or a regulator requires us to keep it for longer.

13.8 **Your rights.** You may ask us at any time, free of charge, what information we hold about you, and you may ask us to correct anything that is wrong. You are also entitled to obtain your own credit record from a credit bureau and to have errors on it corrected.

13.9 **Withdrawing consent.** You may withdraw the consent in clause 13.6 at any time by writing to us. You cannot withdraw the consents in clauses 13.1, 13.2 and 13.5 while money is still owing, because we are legally required to make those enquiries and reports.

13.10 **No group chats.** We will never discuss your account in a WhatsApp group or any other group message.

---

## 14. WHAT YOU ARE ENTITLED TO GET FROM US

14.1 **A free copy of this agreement.** You receive a copy of this signed agreement, free of charge, **before or at the moment we hand you the money** — never later. If the loan is concluded over WhatsApp, we send you the signed PDF before the money goes out.

14.2 **A statement of account, on request.** At any time, you may ask us for a written statement showing every charge we have levied, every payment you have made, and the balance outstanding. The statement is free. If you later want a **duplicate** of a statement we have already given you, we may charge for it, but **never more than N$2.00 per page**.

14.3 **A paid-up letter.** When you settle in full we will give you a paid-up letter free of charge, without you having to ask, confirming that nothing further is owed. We will also cancel any debit order mandate and tell the credit bureaus in clause 13.3 that the account is settled.

14.4 **A settlement quote.** Free, at any time, on request (clause 7.5).

14.5 **The law, in writing.** Copies of the Microlending Act 7 of 2018, the regulations and the NAMFISA standards, our complaints procedure and a complaint form are kept at our office and we will show them to you or give you a copy on request, free of charge.

14.6 **An explanation.** We must explain this agreement to you in a language you understand, and give you the chance to read it or have it read to you. If you would like anything explained again, at any time during the loan, phone us.

---

## 15. IF YOU ARE UNHAPPY — HOW TO COMPLAIN

15.1 **Step 1 — tell us.** Contact us on +264 81 264 6222 or at erastusmatheus3@gmail.com, or come to our office. Please put the complaint in writing if you can. We will acknowledge it within **5 business days** and give you a written answer within **30 days**.

15.2 **Step 2 — our principal officer.** If you are not satisfied with the answer, ask for the complaint to go to our principal officer, Erastus Taapopi Matheus, at erastusmatheus3@gmail.com. They will respond in writing within a further **14 business days**.

15.3 **Step 3 — NAMFISA.** If you are still not satisfied, you may take the complaint to the Namibia Financial Institutions Supervisory Authority, which regulates us. **We will give you a NAMFISA complaint form free of charge and we will not obstruct or discourage you in any way.**

| NAMFISA | Detail |
|---|---|
| Department | Microlending and Credit Agreements |
| Physical address | 51-55 Werner List Street, Gutenberg Plaza, Windhoek |
| Postal address | P O Box 21250, Windhoek, Namibia |
| Toll-free | 0800 290 500 |
| Email | complaints@namfisa.com.na |

15.4 Complaining costs you nothing and it will never count against you on this loan or on any future application to us.

---

## 16. ADDRESSES FOR NOTICES AND LEGAL DOCUMENTS

16.1 **What *domicilium citandi et executandi* means.** It is the address you formally choose for receiving legal notices and court documents. In plain words: **it is the address where anything official may be delivered to you, and delivery there counts as delivery to you even if you were not there and did not actually collect it.** That is why the address must be correct and must be kept up to date.

16.2 You choose as your *domicilium citandi et executandi* the physical street address in clause 1.2. You confirm that it is a real, physical street address in Namibia at which a person can attend, and not a post box.

16.3 We choose as our *domicilium citandi et executandi* the physical address in clause 1.1.

16.4 **Changing your address.** You may change your chosen address by giving us written notice. The new address must also be a physical street address in Namibia. The change takes effect **10 business days** after we receive the notice.

16.5 **Ordinary notices.** For everything that is not a court document — reminders, statements, settlement quotes, demand letters — you agree that we may also use email, SMS or WhatsApp on the details in clause 1.2. A message sent that way is treated as received on the day it is sent, unless we get a delivery failure. Please tell us straight away if your number changes.

16.6 Court documents and legal process will be delivered only to the address in clause 16.2.

---

## 17. GENERAL TERMS

17.1 **This is the whole agreement.** This agreement, together with the pre-agreement quotation you were given before you signed, the Schedule of Fees and Charges attached as Annexure A, the debit order mandate (if any) attached as Annexure B, any instalment schedule attached as Annexure C, and any Extension Agreement signed under clause 8, is the entire agreement between us. Nothing said before signature that is not written in these documents forms part of it.

17.2 **Changes must be in writing and signed by both of us.** No change to this agreement is valid unless it is written down and signed by both you and us — **unless the change reduces what you owe**, in which case it takes effect immediately in your favour. This reflects section 28 of the Microlending Act 7 of 2018. Nobody may change your obligations by phone, by WhatsApp, or by entering something in our app.

17.3 **If we are lenient, we do not lose our rights.** If we allow you extra time or overlook a late payment on one occasion, that does not mean we have given up any right, and it does not change the agreement. Equally, if we have been lenient before, we will give you fair written notice before we stop being lenient.

17.4 **Severability.** If any clause of this agreement is found to be unlawful or unenforceable, that clause is treated as removed and the rest of the agreement remains in force.

17.5 **Transferring this agreement.** We may transfer our rights under this agreement to another registered credit provider, but only on written notice to you, and your rights and the amounts you owe do not change as a result. You may not transfer your obligations to anyone else.

17.6 **Governing law.** This agreement is governed by the law of the Republic of Namibia, in particular the Microlending Act 7 of 2018, the regulations and NAMFISA standards made under it, and the Usury Act 73 of 1968.

17.7 **Courts.** In terms of section 45 of the Magistrates' Courts Act 32 of 1944 you consent to a Magistrate's Court having jurisdiction to hear any claim under this agreement **even if the amount claimed is more than the normal limit of that court**. Any claim will be brought in the Magistrate's Court for the district in which you live or work. We do not ask you to consent to being sued in a court that has nothing to do with where you live.

17.8 **Our records.** A certificate signed by our principal officer setting out what you owe is proof of that amount **on the face of it** — meaning a court will accept it as a starting point. **You are free to dispute it**, and if you do, we must prove the amount in the ordinary way. You may ask for the underlying statement of account at any time under clause 14.2.

17.9 **Signing and copies.** This agreement may be signed in two identical originals, one for you and one for us. A signature applied electronically, and a signed copy sent by email or WhatsApp, is as valid as a signature in ink.

17.10 **Meaning of words.** "Business day" means any day except a Saturday, a Sunday or an official Namibian public holiday. "N$" means Namibian Dollars. Headings are for convenience only and do not affect meaning. Words in the singular include the plural, and the other way round.

# ANNEXURE A — SCHEDULE OF FEES AND CHARGES

**Attached to and forming part of the Microloan Agreement**

This schedule lists **every** amount QuickServe Cashloan may charge you. If a charge is not on this list, you do not owe it. The exact Namibian Dollar figures for your own loan are in the cost table in clause 2 of your Microloan Agreement — this schedule explains what each charge is and what limits apply to it.

---

## 1. THE ONE RULE THAT CAPS EVERYTHING

1.1 Namibian law treats **every amount you owe us that is not the cash we handed you** as a "finance charge". Interest is a finance charge. The service fee is a finance charge. Anything added when a due date is extended is a finance charge.

1.2 For a short-term microloan repayable within five months, **the total of all finance charges may not exceed 30% of the principal** — the cash actually advanced to you. This is the maximum determined by the Registrar under the Usury Act 73 of 1968 and applied by the Microlending Act 7 of 2018.

1.3 **The 30% is once-off for the whole loan. It is not 30% per month, not 30% per week, and not 30% again each time a due date is extended.**

1.4 The service fee is counted **inside** the 30%, never on top of it.

1.5 If any amount we ever charge exceeds the legal maximum, that excess is void, you do not owe it, and if you have paid it we refund it.

---

## 2. WHAT WE CHARGE

| # | Charge | How it works | Limit |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2.1 | **Interest** | A flat percentage of the principal, calculated **once** for the whole loan period. It does not compound and it does not grow month by month. | Together with 2.2, never more than 30% of the principal |
| 2.2 | **Service fee** | A single flat amount, charged once at the start of the loan. It covers the cost of assessing and administering your loan. | Together with 2.1, never more than 30% of the principal |
| 2.3 | **Total finance charges (2.1 + 2.2)** | The complete cost of borrowing from us when you repay on time. | **Never more than 30% of the principal** |
| 2.4 | **Charge on an extension of the due date** | Only if you ask for an extension and we both sign an Extension Agreement. It is calculated on the principal still outstanding, at the rate in your agreement. | Only whatever room is left under the 30% ceiling — **which may be nil** |
| 2.5 | **Default interest** | Only if you miss the due date and no extension has been signed. Charged on the amount outstanding, and it stops the day you pay. | **Not more than [DEFAULT INTEREST RATE — NOT MORE THAN 5]% per month, for not more than 3 months in total.** After 3 months, no further default interest at all |
| 2.6 | **Duplicate statement of account** | Your statement is free. This applies only if you ask for a second copy of a statement we have already given you. | **Never more than N$2.00 per page** |
| 2.7 | **Returned or failed debit order** | We recover only the amount the bank actually charges us, shown on your statement with the bank's own reference. We add nothing of our own to it. | Actual bank cost only, itemised, and counted inside the 30% ceiling |
| 2.8 | **Legal and collection costs** | Only if we have to enforce the agreement through an attorney or a court, and only after we have given you the written notices required by clause 9 of your agreement. On the attorney-and-own-client scale. | Only costs actually incurred, **always subject to assessment by the court or the taxing master** |

---

## 3. WHAT WE NEVER CHARGE

| We do not charge for | |
|---|---|
| Applying for a loan | **N$0.00** |
| Being assessed or credit-checked | **N$0.00** |
| A settlement quote | **N$0.00** |
| Settling your loan early — there is **no early settlement penalty**, and the finance charges are reduced pro rata | **N$0.00** |
| Cancelling within the 3-business-day cooling-off period (you pay only the days you had the money) | **N$0.00** |
| Your copy of the signed loan agreement | **N$0.00** |
| Your first copy of any statement of account | **N$0.00** |
| A breakdown showing how your payments were applied | **N$0.00** |
| Your paid-up letter when you settle | **N$0.00** |
| A copy of your affordability assessment | **N$0.00** |
| Reminder calls, SMSs or WhatsApp messages | **N$0.00** |
| A NAMFISA complaint form, or lodging a complaint | **N$0.00** |
| The revenue stamp on the original agreement — **we pay this, not you** | **N$0.00** |
| Insurance — **we may not and do not make any insurance a condition of a loan** | **N$0.00** |

---

## 4. WHAT LOANS COST — ILLUSTRATION

These are illustrations at the legal ceiling, using a 30-day loan with interest at 25% of the principal and a service fee. **Your actual figures are in clause 2 of your Microloan Agreement.**

| Cash you receive | Interest (25%) | Service fee | Total finance charges | As % of principal | **Total you repay on the due date** |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| N$500.00 | N$125.00 | N$25.00 | N$150.00 | 30.0% | **N$650.00** |
| N$1,000.00 | N$250.00 | N$50.00 | N$300.00 | 30.0% | **N$1,300.00** |
| N$2,000.00 | N$500.00 | N$100.00 | N$600.00 | 30.0% | **N$2,600.00** |
| N$3,000.00 | N$750.00 | N$150.00 | N$900.00 | 30.0% | **N$3,900.00** |
| N$5,000.00 | N$1,250.00 | N$250.00 | N$1,500.00 | 30.0% | **N$6,500.00** |

**Read the last column.** That is the single figure you must have ready on the due date.

---

## 5. IF YOU PAY EARLY, YOU PAY LESS

5.1 The finance charges are reduced in proportion to the days you actually had the money. Using the N$1,000.00 example above, where the full-term finance charges are N$300.00 over 30 days:

| Day 10 | N$100.00 | N$1,100.00 | N$200.00 |

| Day 30 (due date) | N$300.00 | N$1,300.00 | — |

5.2 Phone or WhatsApp **+264 81 264 6222** for a free written settlement quote before you pay.

---

## 6. CHANGES TO THIS SCHEDULE

6.1 We may change this schedule for **future** loans.

6.2 **The figures in your signed Microloan Agreement do not change.** A change to this schedule can never increase what you owe on a loan you have already signed for. Under clause 17.2 of your agreement, nothing that increases your liability is valid unless it is written down and signed by both of us.

6.3 The current schedule is displayed at our office and is given to every borrower with every agreement, free of charge.

7.1 Ask us first: **+264 81 264 6222** or erastusmatheus3@gmail.com.
