# CONSENT AND PRIVACY NOTICE

**How QuickServe Cashloan collects, uses, shares, stores and protects your personal information**

Version [1.0] — issued [DATE] — application / account number [LOAN OR ACCOUNT NUMBER]

| | |
|---|---|
| **Applicant / Borrower** | [FULL NAME AS ON NAMIBIAN ID] |
| **Namibian ID number** | [ID NUMBER] |
| **Date this notice was given to you** | [DATE] |
| **Given to you by** | [NAME OF QUICKSERVE STAFF MEMBER] |

---

## 1. WHY YOU ARE READING THIS

1.1 To lend you money lawfully, we must collect and keep personal information about you. This notice tells you what we collect, why we need it, who else sees it, where it is kept, how long we keep it, and what you may demand from us.

1.2 We give you this notice **before** you sign the loan agreement, so that you decide with the facts in front of you.

1.3 Please read it. If anything is unclear, ask. We will explain it in a language you understand, and we will read it to you if you prefer. Nothing important is hidden in small print.

1.4 This notice forms part of your loan file. You keep the original. We keep a signed copy.

## 2. WHO IS RESPONSIBLE FOR YOUR INFORMATION

| | |
|---|---|
| **Registered legal name** | Quickserve Financial Services CC |
| **Trading as** | QuickServe Cashloan |
| **Business registration number** | CC/2026/01904 |
| **Physical address** | 3403 Danger Ashipala Street, Swakopmund, Namibia |
| **Telephone / WhatsApp** | +264 81 264 6222 |
| **Email** | erastusmatheus3@gmail.com |
| **Person responsible for your information** | [FULL NAME], [POSITION — NORMALLY THE PRINCIPAL OFFICER] |

2.1 The person named in the last row is our **Information Officer**. Every request, question or complaint about your personal information goes to that person.

## 3. THE LAW THIS NOTICE IS BUILT ON

3.1 We must be straight with you about one thing. **Namibia does not currently have a general data protection Act in force.** A Data Protection Bill has been drafted but has not been passed into law, and there is no national data protection authority. We will not quote you a law that does not exist.

3.2 What does protect your information, and what we are bound by, is this:

| Protection | What it means for you |
|---|---|
| Article 13 of the Namibian Constitution | Your privacy, your home and your correspondence are protected. |
| The Microlending Act 7 of 2018 | A microlender may not disclose confidential information obtained in the course of a microlending transaction without your express consent, except that relevant information must be shared with a registered credit bureau. |
| The Credit Bureau Regulations, 2014 (Bank of Namibia) | Credit bureaux are registered and supervised, may release your information to a subscriber only where you have authorised it in writing or the law requires it, and must take reasonable steps to keep the information correct. |
| Your written consent | Set out in section 16 of this notice. You give it knowingly, and you may withdraw it on the terms in section 12. |

3.3 We apply the standards in this notice as a matter of our own policy, whether or not a statute forces us to. If Namibia passes a data protection Act, we will update this notice and tell you.

## 4. WHAT INFORMATION WE COLLECT

| Category | Examples | Why we need it |
|---|---|---|
| Identity | Full name, Namibian ID number, date of birth, copy of your Namibian ID | To confirm you are who you say you are, and to open your account |
| Contact | Mobile number (WhatsApp), email address, physical street address, postal address | To reach you, to send your agreement and statements, and to deliver notices |
| Employment | Employer name, staff or payroll number, workplace address, occupation, latest payslip | To confirm your income and, if it ever becomes necessary, to enforce a court order |
| Financial | Bank name, account number and branch, three months of bank statements, net salary, other loans and monthly commitments | To carry out the affordability assessment the law requires before any loan is granted |
| Credit record | Your credit bureau report and your repayment history with us | A credit bureau check is expected before a microloan is granted |
| Loan account | Amount lent, interest, service fee, issue date, due date, every payment, balance, any extension, default or write-off | To run your account correctly and to keep the accounting records the law requires |
| Next of kin / reference | Name and phone number of one person who can help us reach you | Only to locate you if your own numbers stop working. We do **not** tell that person about your debt |
| Communications | WhatsApp and SMS messages, emails, notes of calls, reminders sent | So there is an honest record of what was said, by both of us |

4.1 We collect only what we need for the purposes in section 6. We collect most of it directly from you. Any credit bureau report is obtained from the bureau itself.

4.2 If you do not give us this information, we cannot lawfully assess or grant the loan. That is not a threat — the affordability assessment and the credit check are legal duties we cannot skip.

4.3 Everything you tell us must be true and complete. A loan granted on false information puts you into debt you cannot carry, which is exactly what the affordability assessment exists to prevent.

## 5. YOUR ORIGINAL DOCUMENTS — WE TAKE COPIES ONLY

5.1 **QuickServe Cashloan does not take, hold, keep or use your bank card, your PIN, any banking password, your original Namibian ID, your original passport, your original driver's licence, or any other original document — not as security, and not to collect a debt.** This is prohibited by section 23(1)(f) of the Microlending Act 7 of 2018.

5.2 We look at your original document, take a copy in front of you, and hand the original straight back to you in the same visit.

5.3 If any person at QuickServe Cashloan ever asks you for your card, your PIN or an original document, **refuse**, and report it — first to our Information Officer, and then to NAMFISA. Our Client Rights and Complaints Charter tells you how.

## 6. WHY WE USE YOUR INFORMATION

| Purpose | What it means in practice |
|---|---|
| Confirming your identity | Checking your ID against the person in front of us |
| Credit bureau enquiry | Where we use a credit bureau, obtaining your credit report before the loan |
| Affordability assessment | Working out from your payslip and three months of bank statements whether you can repay without hardship |
| Preparing your paperwork | Producing your written quotation, your loan agreement and your statements |
| Paying out and running the loan | Transferring the money, recording payments, calculating the balance |
| Reminders and statements | Sending you a message before the due date and a statement when you ask |
| Collecting what is owed | Contacting you, sending a written demand, and — only after written notice to you — handing the account to a debt collector or lawyer |
| Credit bureau reporting | Where we use a credit bureau, reporting how the account performs, good and bad |
| Regulatory compliance | NAMFISA, our auditor or accounting officer, and the Namibia Revenue Agency |
| Proper accounting records | Keeping the record of money advanced, charges raised, payments received and amounts outstanding that the law requires us to keep |
| Marketing (optional) | Telling you about our products — **only if you tick yes** in section 16 |

6.1 We will not use your information for any other purpose without asking you first.

## 7. WHO WE SHARE IT WITH

| Who | What they get | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Registered credit bureaux we use, if any — [COMPUSCAN CREDIT REFERENCE BUREAU (PTY) LTD] and [TRANSUNION CREDIT BUREAU NAMIBIA (PTY) LTD] | Your identity details and how your account performs, including on-time payments and missed payments | Where a bureau is used: a credit check is expected before the loan, and reporting afterwards |
| NAMFISA | Your file, if it is requested in connection with a complaint or an investigation | NAMFISA is the microlending regulator in Namibia |
| Our attorney or debt collector | Your file, only if the account goes into serious default | To recover the debt — and only after we have given you written notice that we intend to hand the account over |
| Our bank and the payment system | Your account details and the amount to be collected | To pay the loan out and to collect an agreed debit order |
| Our auditor, accounting officer or bookkeeper | Your account records | To audit and report on our books. They are bound to confidentiality |
| Namibia Revenue Agency | Only what tax law requires | Legal duty |
| Your employer | **Only** confirmation that you work there and that the payslip is genuine | To verify your income. We do **not** discuss your loan, your balance or your arrears with your employer |
| A court | Your file | Only if legal proceedings become necessary |

7.1 We do **not** sell your information to anyone, ever.

7.2 We do **not** post about your debt on Facebook, WhatsApp status, or anywhere else public.

7.3 We do **not** discuss your account in any WhatsApp group.

7.4 We do **not** tell your family, your neighbours, your colleagues, your landlord or your church that you owe us money.

## 8. CREDIT BUREAU REPORTING — WHAT IT ACTUALLY MEANS FOR YOU

8.1 The law expects a microlender to check an applicant's credit record with a registered credit bureau before lending. Where we use a credit bureau, we obtain your credit report from it before we lend.

8.2 Where we report to a credit bureau, we report your account while the loan runs and after it ends. That includes the **good** — that you paid on time — and the **bad** — that you paid late or did not pay. A clean record with us makes it easier for you to borrow elsewhere. A poor one makes it harder.

8.3 If we ever mark a balance as unrecoverable in our own books (a "write-off"), that is an internal accounting step only. **It does not cancel your debt**, and the payment history already reported to the bureau stays on your record. We will not report a written-off or compromised debt as though it were paid in full, because that would be untrue.

8.4 When you settle in full, we give you a **free** paid-up letter, without you having to ask; and if we have reported this account to a credit bureau, we submit your paid-up status to that bureau. Where a bureau was used, the letter tells you which bureau and on what date.

8.5 You may obtain your own credit report from the bureau and ask for corrections. If we reported something about you that is wrong, tell our Information Officer, give us the proof, and we will submit the correction to the credit bureau within [10] business days and confirm this to you in writing. The bureau then updates its own records in its own time — how quickly it does so is not within our control, but our part is done within that period.

## 9. WHERE YOUR INFORMATION IS KEPT — OUR LOAN BOOK RUNS ON A DEVICE, NOT A SERVER

9.1 You should know how our records are actually held, because it is unusual and it affects you.

9.2 Our loan book is an app that runs on a business device — a phone or tablet held by QuickServe Cashloan. **All client records are stored in that device's own storage.** There is no central server. Your information is not uploaded to an internet database, not stored in a cloud system, and not accessible over the internet by anyone.

9.3 **The good side.** There is no online database of our clients for anyone to hack. Your information is not sitting on a website. It does not travel to anyone except the people named in section 7.

9.4 **The risk, stated honestly.** If that device is lost, stolen, damaged or its storage is cleared, records can be lost or could reach the wrong hands. We manage that risk as follows:

| Control | What we do |
|---|---|
| Device lock | The device has its own screen lock and passcode. |
| App lock | The loan book app is protected by a separate passcode, asked every time the app is opened. The passcode is stored in scrambled (hashed) form, not as plain text. |
| Who may use it | Only [NUMBER] named person(s) have the device passcode and the app passcode: [NAME(S) AND POSITION(S)]. |
| Custody | The device stays with the [PRINCIPAL OFFICER / OWNER]. It is not lent out, not shared, and not left unattended. |
| Backups | A backup of the loan book is taken at least [WEEKLY] and kept at [WHERE THE BACKUP IS KEPT]. |
| Encrypted backups | Any backup that leaves the device — to cloud storage, email or a chat — is encrypted first, using AES-GCM encryption with a key derived from a passphrase. An unencrypted backup is never placed in cloud storage or a chat. |
| Backup passphrase | Known only to [NAME AND POSITION]. It is never stored together with the backup file. |
| Paper files | Your signed agreement, quotation, ID copy, payslip and bank statements are kept in a locked cabinet at our physical address, accessible only to [NAME(S) AND POSITION(S)]. |

9.5 **Your signed paper documents remain the authoritative record.** The app is how we run the account day to day; the signed originals are what govern it.

9.6 **If something goes wrong.** If the device is lost or stolen, or we otherwise have reason to believe your information has been exposed, we will tell you in writing as soon as we reasonably can after we discover it, tell you what information was affected and what we are doing about it, and report the incident to NAMFISA. We promise this as a matter of our own policy — no Namibian law currently requires it of us.

## 10. HOW LONG WE KEEP YOUR INFORMATION

10.1 It is our policy to keep your signed loan agreement, your quotation, your affordability assessment, your ID copy, your payslip, your bank statements, your payment records, any extension agreement and our correspondence with you for at least **five (5) years after your account is finally settled or otherwise closed**.

10.2 After that period we destroy the records securely: paper is shredded, and electronic records are deleted from the device and from all backups.

10.3 This five-year period is **our own internal policy**, not a figure we are quoting from a statute. Where NAMFISA standards, tax law, or a court order require us to keep a record for longer, the longer period applies.

10.4 We chose five years because the Microlending Act contemplates that a microlender's records may be inspected, tax law requires us to keep books, and an ordinary contractual debt in Namibia prescribes three years after it falls due under the Prescription Act 68 of 1969 — with the clock starting afresh each time the debt is acknowledged.

## 11. YOUR RIGHTS OVER YOUR INFORMATION

| Your right | What you may demand |
|---|---|
| To be told | To know what we hold about you, why, and who we give it to. That is what this notice does. |
| A free copy of what you signed | A copy of your signed loan agreement, free of charge, before or at the time the money is paid to you. |
| A statement of account | A statement showing every charge levied, every payment made and the balance outstanding. Duplicates may be charged for, but not more than [N$2.00] per page. |
| To see what we hold | To ask our Information Officer, in writing, for the personal information we hold about you. We will respond within [10] business days, free of charge. |
| To correct it | To have wrong or out-of-date information corrected. Tell us and we will fix it, and submit a correction to the credit bureau if we reported it. |
| To withdraw consent | On the terms in section 12 below. |
| To refuse marketing | To say no to marketing, or to change your mind later, with no effect at all on your loan or on any future application. |
| To complain | Free of charge, first to us and then to NAMFISA. See our Client Rights and Complaints Charter. |

11.1 Exercising any of these rights costs you nothing, except the per-page charge for a duplicate statement.

## 12. WITHDRAWING YOUR CONSENT

12.1 You may withdraw your consent at any time by writing to our Information Officer. We will confirm receipt in writing.

12.2 You must understand the limits, and we would rather you knew them now than felt misled later:

12.2.1 Withdrawal works from the day we receive it. It cannot undo something already lawfully done.

12.2.2 We must still keep the records described in section 10, because the law requires us to keep them.

12.2.3 While you still owe us money, we may still use your information to run and collect the account, and where we report to a credit bureau we may continue to report the account. Withdrawing consent does not stop lawful credit-bureau reporting and does not cancel the debt.

12.2.4 If you withdraw your consent **before** the loan is granted, we cannot grant it, because we may not lend without a credit check and an affordability assessment.

12.2.5 You may always withdraw consent to **marketing** with no consequences whatsoever.

## 13. HOW WE WILL CONTACT YOU

13.1 We contact you by WhatsApp, SMS, telephone call or email, using the details you gave us.

13.2 We will never discuss your account in a group chat.

13.3 We will not discuss your account with anyone who answers your phone, unless you have told us in writing that we may speak to that person.

13.5 We contact you between [08:00 AND 17:00 MONDAY TO FRIDAY] and [08:00 AND 13:00 ON SATURDAY]. We do not contact you on Sundays or public holidays, unless you have asked us to.

13.6 Tell us within [5] business days if your phone number, address, employer or bank account changes. If we cannot reach you, notices sent to the last details you gave us still count as delivered.

## 14. COMPLAINTS

14.1 If you are unhappy with how we have handled your information, complain — it is free, and we will not treat you differently for it.

14.2 Step one is our Information Officer, in writing. Step two is NAMFISA. The full procedure, with timeframes and contact details, is in our **Client Rights and Complaints Charter**, which we give you together with this notice.

# DEBIT ORDER AND PAYMENT AUTHORITY MANDATE

**Authority to collect an agreed amount from your bank account on an agreed date**

Mandate number [MANDATE NUMBER] — linked to loan agreement number [LOAN AGREEMENT NUMBER]

> **This is not a new loan and it does not add any cost.** It is only your instruction to your bank to pay us what you already agreed to pay under your loan agreement. Signing it is your choice. You may also repay by bank transfer or in cash at our office.

## 1. THE PARTIES

## 2. THE LOAN THIS MANDATE RELATES TO

2.1 These figures are taken from your signed loan agreement and your written quotation. They do not change because you signed this mandate.

## 3. YOUR BANK ACCOUNT

3.1 You confirm that this account is in your own name and that you are entitled to authorise payments from it.

## 4. WHAT YOU ARE AUTHORISING US TO COLLECT

| | |
|---|---|
| Amount of each collection | N$ [AMOUNT] |
| Date of the first collection | [DATE] |
| How often | [ONCE ONLY / MONTHLY ON THE SAME DATE] |
| Number of collections | [NUMBER] |
| Date of the last collection | [DATE] |
| **Maximum total that may be collected under this mandate** | **N$ [AMOUNT]** |

4.1 You authorise QuickServe Cashloan to instruct your bank to pay the amount(s) set out above from your account on the date(s) set out above, and you instruct your bank to act on those instructions.

4.2 **The total collected under this mandate may never exceed what you owe under the loan agreement, and may never exceed the maximum total stated above.**

## 5. HOW COLLECTION WORKS

5.1 We collect only through a payment system and payment instrument registered with the Bank of Namibia. We do not use any other method to take money from your account.

5.2 If a collection date falls on a Saturday, Sunday or public holiday, we will present the collection on the **first business day after** that date, unless you ask us in writing to present it on the last business day before instead. We will not present it before its stated date without your written request.

5.3 We will not split a collection into several smaller amounts, and we will not present it more often than this mandate allows, unless you agree in writing.

5.4 Your bank will show the collection on your statement under the name in clause 1.

## 6. IF A COLLECTION DOES NOT GO THROUGH

6.1 If a collection fails because there is not enough money in your account, we may present it **once more**, within [10] business days, and we will send you a message first to tell you the date we intend to present it.

6.2 We will not present it again after that without speaking to you and agreeing a new date in writing.

6.3 **We do not charge you a fee for a failed collection.** Your own bank may charge you its own fee — that is between you and your bank, and we receive none of it.

6.4 A failed collection does not by itself put you in default if you pay us by another means by the due date.

## 7. THE LIMITS ON THIS MANDATE

7.1 We may not increase the amount, add a collection, or change the date without your written agreement, signed by both of us. This mandate cannot be varied by a phone call, a message or a note in our system.

7.2 This mandate covers only the loan agreement identified in clause 2. It does not cover any future loan. A new loan needs a new mandate.

7.3 This mandate gives us no right to any other account of yours.

7.4 This mandate is **not** an open-ended authority to keep checking your account and collecting whenever money appears.

## 8. THIS MANDATE IS NOT SECURITY, AND WE HOLD NOTHING OF YOURS

8.1 This mandate is a payment instruction. It is not security for the loan and it gives us no rights over anything you own.

8.2 QuickServe Cashloan does not take, hold or use your bank card, your PIN, your banking password, your original Namibian ID, your original passport or your original driver's licence — not as security and not for collection. That conduct is prohibited by section 23(1)(f) of the Microlending Act 7 of 2018. If anyone asks you for these, refuse and report it to NAMFISA.

## 9. YOUR RIGHT TO CANCEL OR CHANGE THIS MANDATE

9.1 **You may cancel this mandate at any time.** You do not need a reason and we will not treat you differently for doing it.

9.2 To cancel, give us written notice — a letter, an email to erastusmatheus3@gmail.com or a WhatsApp message to +264 81 264 6222 is enough. Please give us at least **[3] business days' notice before the next collection date**, so that we can stop the instruction in time.

9.3 You may also instruct your own bank to stop the debit order. If you do, please tell us too, so that we do not present a collection that will be rejected.

9.4 We will confirm your cancellation in writing within **[2] business days** of receiving it.

9.5 To change the amount or the date, sign a new mandate with us. We will replace this one and give you a free copy of the new one.

## 10. CANCELLING THIS MANDATE DOES NOT CANCEL YOUR LOAN

10.1 This is the most important sentence on this page. **Cancelling or stopping the debit order does not cancel, reduce or suspend what you owe under the loan agreement.** The debt stays.

10.2 If you cancel the mandate, you must still pay the amount owing by the due date, by bank transfer or in cash at our office.

10.3 Money already lawfully collected while this mandate was in force is not refundable simply because you later cancelled the mandate.

## 11. IF WE COLLECT THE WRONG AMOUNT

11.1 If we collect an amount you did not authorise, or more than you owe, tell us at once. We will investigate and, where we were wrong, **refund the amount to your account within [5] business days**, without you having to ask twice.

11.2 You may also dispute an unauthorised or incorrect debit directly with your own bank, within the period your bank allows. Nothing in this mandate takes that right away.

11.3 If we caused you a bank charge by collecting in error, we will refund that charge too.

## 12. WHEN THIS MANDATE COMES TO AN END

12.1 This mandate ends automatically on the earliest of:

12.1.1 the date you have paid everything owing under the loan agreement;

12.1.2 the last collection date stated in clause 4; or

12.1.3 the date your cancellation takes effect under clause 9.

12.2 **When your loan is settled in full we will cancel this mandate with our bank within [2] business days and confirm the cancellation to you in writing.** We will present no further collections after settlement. If you settle early or pay the balance off in one payment, the same applies.

12.3 If you settle early, your finance charges are reduced in proportion to the days you actually had the loan, as your loan agreement provides, and we will collect only the reduced settlement amount.

## 13. THIS IS NOT A SALARY DEDUCTION AUTHORITY

13.1 This mandate operates only against the bank account named in clause 3.

13.2 It does **not** authorise your employer to deduct anything from your salary, and it does not authorise us to approach your employer for a deduction. Any salary deduction would require a separate written authority signed by you, and would be subject to the limits in the Labour Act 11 of 2007.

## 14. YOUR DECLARATION

I confirm that:

1. Every space in this mandate was completely filled in before I signed it. **I did not sign a blank or incomplete document.**
2. This mandate was explained to me in a language I understand, namely **[LANGUAGE]**, by **[NAME OF STAFF MEMBER]**. Interpreter, if any: **[NAME OF INTERPRETER OR "NONE"]**.
3. I read this mandate myself ☐ **or** it was read to me ☐.
4. The bank account details in clause 3 are correct and the account is mine.
5. I understand that I may cancel this mandate at any time, and that cancelling it does not cancel my debt.
6. I received a copy of this signed mandate, free of charge, on the day I signed it.
7. Signing this mandate was my choice. I was told I could instead pay by bank transfer or in cash at the QuickServe office.
